aggressive_definition: High-grade prostate cancer defined broadly as Gleason score 7 to 10; Gleason score 8 to 10 was also analyzed as a more restrictive high-grade endpoint.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The odds ratios for a linear increase in lycopene (per 10 μg/dL) were 0.99 (95% CI: 0.94-1.04), 1.01 (0.94-1.08), and 1.02 (0.90-1.15) for Gleason 2 to 6, 7 to 10, and 8 to 10, respectively.
study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the Prostate Cancer Prevention Trial
reason: Cancer was ascertained by biopsy during a prevention trial, and the nested case-control analysis reported both prostate cancer generally and incident high-grade endpoints defined by Gleason score.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: The odds ratios for a linear increase in lycopene (per 10 μg/dL) were 0.99 (95% CI: 0.94-1.04), 1.01 (0.94-1.08), and 1.02 (0.90-1.15) for Gleason 2 to 6, 7 to 10, and 8 to 10, respectively.
estimate_classifications.reason: The row's OR of 0.99 corresponds specifically to Gleason 2 to 6 prostate cancer, a low-grade/nonaggressive endpoint.

additional_estimates.comparison: Per 10 μg/dL increase in serum lycopene
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: The odds ratios for a linear increase in lycopene (per 10 μg/dL) were 0.99 (95% CI: 0.94-1.04), 1.01 (0.94-1.08), and 1.02 (0.90-1.15) for Gleason 2 to 6, 7 to 10, and 8 to 10, respectively.
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: There were 1,683 cases (461 Gleason score ≥ 7, 125 Gleason score ≥ 8) and 1,751 controls.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
